title: Krylov Complexity and Entropy of Composite Quantum Systems
authors: Jeff Murugan, Victor Van Aswegen, Hendrik J R Van Zyl
abstract: We investigate the behaviour of Krylov complexity as the number of degrees of freedom of a quantum system increases. Specifically, we show that for tensor products of commuting subsystems, the leading excess complexity is controlled by a weighted variance of the subsystem Lanczos coefficients. This provides a quantitative measure of dynamical heterogeneity and a precise characterization of synchronous evolution. We also show that Krylov entropy is able to disambiguate the information associated with subsystems composition from that generated by dynamical mismatch, and that the same Lanczos variance controls the leading mismatch contribution to both complexity and the entropy. Our results establish excess complexity and Krylov entropy as complementary probes of the emergence of collective dynamics in large quantum systems.
summary: This paper develops and applies Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy to quantify how the dynamics of a composite quantum system deviates from the simple sum of its parts. It establishes that this excess non-additivity is precisely controlled by the weighted variance of the subsystem Lanczos coefficients. These measures offer complementary theoretical probes for understanding collective dynamics and synchronization in many-body quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-additive behavior of quantum dynamics in composite systems by analyzing excess complexity and Krylov entropy.
main_result: Excess complexity and Krylov entropy are shown to be controlled by the weighted variance of subsystem Lanczos coefficients, providing complementary measures of dynamical heterogeneity and the deviation from synchronous evolution.
method: The analysis uses early-time expansions of Krylov complexity and entropy, relating them to the Lanczos coefficients derived from the system's Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The study uses general composite quantum systems, with the Kitaev chain serving as a detailed test case analyzed in momentum space.
key_observables: Krylov Complexity ($C(t)$), Excess Complexity ($\Delta C(t)$), Krylov Entropy ($S_K(t)$), and the entropy difference ($\Delta S_K(t)$).
important_parameters: Time ($t$), system size ($L$), and the weighted variance of Lanczos coefficients ($	ext{Var}_w(a_{1,i})$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on early-time expansions and specific algebraic structures (like the Heisenberg-Weyl algebra) to derive explicit formulas for the leading order terms.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows extensive scaling of excess complexity per site for the Kitaev chain; Figure 2 compares combined and product Krylov entropies, showing a negative deficit ($\Delta S_K < 0$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the diagnostics (complexity/entropy), deriving the leading order behavior using Lanczos coefficients, and then comparing the excess terms ($\Delta C(t)$ and $\Delta S_K(t)$) to show they are governed by the same variance term.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, quantifiable tools (complexity and entropy measures) to diagnose non-equilibrium dynamics and the emergence of collective behavior in large quantum systems, which is central to understanding many-body physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Excess Krylov complexity per site for the Kitaev chain with µ = J = ∆= 1 and several system sizes. The approximate collapse of the curves demonstrates the extensive scaling of the excess complexity beyond the strict early-time regime.

Figure 2: Difference between the entropy of the combined Lanczos chain and the product Krylov entropy, ∆S K = S comb K −S prod K , per site for the Kitaev chain with µ = J = ∆= 1. The negative entropy difference at early and intermediate times reflects the compression of subsystem-resolved Krylov information by the combined Lanczos construction. Its increasing magnitude with system size is consistent with the L log L enhancement of the leading short-time contribu- tion.
